title: A Autopsy for the Alibi
premise: Beatrix Hartwell built a quiet life in Saltmere Bay archiving the town's oldest wound: the 1998 disappearance of heiress Cordelia Vane, whose body was never found. When an anonymous confession letter arrives postmarked the day after matriarch Eleanor Vane's funeral, Beatrix realizes the letter's sender knew details only the killer could know—and that the funeral itself was the trigger. Following a coded ledger hidden in the Vane family's tide tables and gravestone inscriptions, Beatrix uncovers an inheritance scheme in which Cordelia's 'disappearance' was staged to redirect the estate, and her own late mother was complicit. In the climax, at low tide beneath the old pier, Beatrix confronts the surviving conspirator—Eleanor's lawyer and secret son—who confesses that Cordelia died accidentally during the staging and that Beatrix's mother helped bury the truth to protect her daughter from the Vane family's reach. The ledger is surrendered, the case finally closes, and Beatrix, no longer invisible, chooses to stay in Saltmere Bay on her own terms.
about_author: Freya Nakamura is a former coastal archivist who spent a decade cataloguing maritime estates before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about small towns that keep their secrets the way the sea keeps its dead—patiently, and never quite forever.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of the Dead
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Establishes her meticulous archive of the Cordelia Vane case and her deliberately small life in Saltmere Bay. Emotional beat: controlled loneliness disguised as order.

chapters.title: Postmarked Yesterday
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. A confession letter arrives dated the day after Eleanor Vane's funeral—impossible timing. It names no one but quotes details never made public. Beat: dread cracking through routine.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Beatrix's POV. How she came to Saltmere Bay after her mother's death and why she chose this case. Beat: grief as origin story.

chapters.title: The Funeral She Missed
chapters.summary: Beatrix attends the wake uninvited, watching the Vane heirs perform mourning. Secondhand tension with cousin Ambrose Vane. Beat: outsider's hunger to belong.

chapters.title: What the Letter Knew
chapters.summary: Beatrix cross-references the letter against her files; three details match sealed evidence. Beat: the cold case turns warm and dangerous.

chapters.title: Ambrose at the Door
chapters.summary: Ambrose Vane visits, probing whether she received anything 'of Eleanor's.' POV alternates briefly to his polished menace. Beat: first direct threat.

chapters.title: Tide Tables
chapters.summary: Beatrix notices the letter's phrasing mirrors marginalia in Eleanor's tide almanacs, donated to the archive. Beat: the hunt becomes intellectual obsession.

chapters.title: The Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Decoding begins: dates in the almanac correspond to tides, and tides to numbers. Beat: exhilaration shadowed by paranoia—someone has been in her office.

chapters.title: Harriet's Warning
chapters.summary: POV Harriet Okafor, Beatrix's landlady and former Vane housekeeper. She warns Beatrix off, revealing Eleanor burned papers before dying. Beat: loyalty versus fear.

chapters.title: Chapter and Verse
chapters.summary: Beatrix maps ledger entries onto gravestone inscriptions; each verse marks a date and a payment. Beat: the conspiracy acquires architecture.

chapters.title: The Lawyer's Son
chapters.summary: Research reveals estate lawyer Gerald Pike had a son born the same year as Cordelia—a hidden heir. Beat: inheritance motive crystallizes.

chapters.title: Episode Ninety-One
chapters.summary: Beatrix records a podcast episode hinting at new evidence, deliberately baiting the killer. Beat: agency reclaimed, risk invited.

chapters.title: Someone Listens Back
chapters.summary: A second letter arrives: 'Stop, or the tide gives up what it took.' POV Beatrix. Beat: fear sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: Cordelia's Summer
chapters.summary: Interlude, Cordelia's reconstructed voice via diary excerpts Beatrix reads. The heiress planned to disinherit everyone. Beat: victim becomes person.

chapters.title: The Pier at Low Water
chapters.summary: Beatrix scouts the pier referenced by ledger coordinates; finds a hollow stanchion, recently disturbed. Beat: physical danger enters the story.

chapters.title: Ambrose's Alibi
chapters.summary: Beatrix interviews Ambrose; his alibi for 1998 is airtight—too airtight, rehearsed. Beat: cat-and-mouse over tea.

chapters.title: Mother's Handwriting
chapters.summary: Devastating discovery: marginalia in the almanac matches her mother's hand. Beat: betrayal at the center of her own past.

chapters.title: The Archive Burns
chapters.summary: Arson destroys part of the town records office; Beatrix's duplicate files survive by luck. POV includes young volunteer Milo. Beat: escalation, stakes made real.

chapters.title: Harriet Breaks
chapters.summary: Harriet admits she saw Eleanor and Gerald Pike with a trunk on the pier in 1998 and stayed silent for money. Beat: complicity as survival.

chapters.title: The Staging Theory
chapters.summary: Beatrix assembles it: Cordelia's disappearance was staged to void her will and reroute the estate through probate. Beat: revelation's cold logic.

chapters.title: But She Didn't Leave
chapters.summary: Forensic re-reading shows Cordelia never reached the ferry; the staging went wrong. Someone died that night. Beat: mystery hardens into murder.

chapters.title: Milo Follows Someone
chapters.summary: Teenage Milo tails a figure photographing Beatrix's office; loses them but gets a partial plate. Beat: the hunted gains allies.

chapters.title: Gerald Pike's Office
chapters.summary: Beatrix breaks into the closed law office; finds the original will and a second ledger key. Beat: trespass, triumph, terror.

chapters.title: The Second Son
chapters.summary: DNA-era records suggest Gerald's son inherited under a false name—and lives in Saltmere Bay still. Beat: the killer is a neighbor.

chapters.title: Suspects in a Small Town
chapters.summary: Beatrix audits every man of the right age; suspicion poisons her friendships. Beat: belonging curdles into distrust.

chapters.title: The Tide Gives Up a Shoe
chapters.summary: Storm erosion exposes a rotted shoe and a locket under the pier—Cordelia's monogram. Beat: the sea returns what it took.

chapters.title: Police at Last
chapters.summary: Detective Ilsa Reyes arrives from the county; skeptical, then convinced by the locket chain of custody. Beat: uneasy alliance.

chapters.title: Exhumation Order
chapters.summary: The grave labeled Cordelia Vane is opened; it holds no one—or rather, holds stones and a stranger's coat buttons. Beat: the town's founding lie exposed.

chapters.title: Eleanor's Letters
chapters.summary: Hidden correspondence shows Eleanor orchestrated the staging and paid Gerald for decades. Beat: power's corruption laid bare.

chapters.title: They Know You Know
chapters.summary: Beatrix's home is searched while she's out; the letter is gone. Reyes assigns protection. Beat: siege mentality.

chapters.title: The Trap at the Boathouse
chapters.summary: Beatrix leaks false ledger coordinates to flush the killer; a figure takes the bait but escapes. Beat: hunter and hunted trade places.

chapters.title: Partial Plate, Full Name
chapters.summary: Milo's photo plus the plate identifies Gerald's son: Martin Hale, the town's beloved harbormaster. Beat: shock wearing a familiar face.

chapters.title: Martin Hale Invites Her Sailing
chapters.summary: Hale, aware he's suspected, lures Beatrix onto his boat—publicly friendly, privately threatening. Beat: terror in daylight.

chapters.title: What Really Happened in 1998
chapters.summary: Reyes recovers Hale's statement draft: Cordelia caught them mid-staging, fell, died; they buried her beneath the pier and let the sea be blamed. Beat: truth without absolution.

chapters.title: The Confession Letter's Author
chapters.summary: Handwriting analysis: the letters were written by dying Gerald Pike, mailed posthumously per his instructions—the funeral triggered the send. Beat: guilt outliving the guilty.

chapters.title: Low Tide, No Moon
chapters.summary: Hale, cornered, goes to move the remains; Beatrix and Reyes follow. Confrontation on the exposed flats; he breaks down rather than fight. Beat: climax—arrest in the mud.

chapters.title: The Ledger Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Courtroom aftermath compressed; the ledger entered as evidence, the estate frozen, Ambrose ruined. Beat: justice as paperwork, satisfying anyway.

chapters.title: Her Mother's Page
chapters.summary: Beatrix reads her mother's final marginal note—an apology, and proof she hid the truth to shield Beatrix from the Vanes. Beat: forgiveness, complicated.

chapters.title: Belonging
chapters.summary: Epilogue-adjacent: the town, stripped of its myth, awkwardly makes room for Beatrix; Harriet, Milo, Reyes become her people. Beat: chosen belonging.

chapters.title: Case Closed, Archive Open
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Beatrix's POV. She records the last episode, then shelves the alphabetized file and starts a blank notebook. Beat: peace—not invisibility, but presence.
